key_insight: High within-dataset accuracy masked weaker cross-dataset performance: EfficientNet-B0 generalised best at 78.4%, while ShuffleNetV2 fell to 66.2%.
clinical_relevance: MRI tumour classifiers need robust external evaluation before their reported accuracy can inform expectations for clinical use.
method: Compared six deep learning architectures across healthy, meningioma, glioma and pituitary tumour MRI classes.
Combined four public datasets, removing exact and near-duplicates and grouping visually similar images for 5-fold cross-validation.
Tested cross-dataset generalisation using leave-one-dataset-out evaluation.
evidence_signal: Leakage-aware cross-validation found ShuffleNetV2 (98.41%) and EfficientNet-B0 (98.23%) statistically indistinguishable (p = 0.19), but every model lost accuracy on the held-out dataset.
watch_item: Without patient identifiers, image-similarity grouping cannot guarantee patient-level separation between folds.
paper_title: Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Brain Tumour Classification
